plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Long, fragrant chains of pea-like flowers hang from trained vines. In Japan's wisteria gardens they form glowing tunnels and domes of violet and lavender, and the petals drift down like soft confetti.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April to early May, with peak bloom in many Japanese gardens around the start of May
plants.location: Japan, including the Kawachi Fujien garden in Kitakyushu and Tokyo shrine gardens
plants.funFact: Japanese wisteria twines clockwise, while Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise. Old vines can live for centuries and grow strong enough to crush the trellises that support them.

plants.name: Rhododendron arboreum
plants.description: Himalayan hillsides blaze with clusters of bell-shaped crimson, pink and white blooms on gnarled evergreen trees. Mist-wrapped forests turn into a patchwork of color, and the blooms continue at higher elevations when lower slopes have finished.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February to April at lower elevations, extending into early May at higher elevations
plants.location: Himalayan forests of Nepal, Sikkim and North Bengal
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of Nepal. Its petals are used in local cooking, and its blooms are a familiar sight in the mountain forests.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms in nearly every color stand in neat rows across the flat Dutch countryside. Because bulbs are planted in layers, the display at the Keukenhof gardens continues through the season's final weeks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-March to mid-May, with Keukenhof's display running into the second week of May
plants.location: The Netherlands, including the Keukenhof gardens and the Bollenstreek flower-bulb region
plants.funFact: Tulips are native to the mountains of Central Asia. In the 1600s they became so valuable in Holland that single bulbs sold for the price of a fine house.
